original_question: Define Otto conjugacy on a semigroup S by a ∼o b if there exist elements u and v in S such that au = ub and va = bv. Is there a finite semigroup S for which ∼o is a congruence and the quotient semigroup S/∼o is not cancellative?
target_in_paper: Problem 9.4: Is there a finite semigroup for which ∼o is a congruence and S/∼o is not cancelative? (standard spelling: cancellative). This is the finite version of the Otto-conjugacy/noncancellative-quotient problem, left open after the paper gives an infinite example in Example 6.1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct relation (Otto conjugacy), the correct existence question over semigroups, the added finiteness restriction, the requirement that ∼o be a congruence, and the requirement that the quotient S/∼o be noncancellative. That is essentially the same mathematical target as the paper’s explicit open Problem 9.4. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
missing_details: It helps to say explicitly that S is an arbitrary finite semigroup; the paper does not impose extra hypotheses such as identity, zero, commutativity, embeddability in a group, or epigroup structure for this problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

To make the question fully stand-alone, define “∼o is a congruence” in semigroup terms: whenever x∼ox' and y∼oy', one has xy∼ox'y'. Section 6 recalls exactly this notion before Example 6.1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

It is worth making explicit that S/∼o is the quotient semigroup of ∼o-classes; this quotient is well-defined precisely because ∼o is assumed to be a congruence. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

The phrase “not cancellative” should be unpacked as failure of at least one cancellation law in the quotient (left or right). The paper’s infinite witness in Example 6.1 shows noncancellativity by failure of right cancellation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

Your draft does not indicate that the unrestricted existence problem was already answered positively in the paper by an infinite semigroup, so the genuinely unresolved paper-faithful target is the finite version recorded as Problem 9.4. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
refined_question: Does there exist a finite semigroup S such that the Otto conjugacy relation ∼o on S, defined by a∼ob if and only if there exist u,v∈S with au=ub and va=bv, is a semigroup congruence (that is, x∼ox' and y∼oy' imply xy∼ox'y' for all x,x',y,y'∈S), and such that the quotient semigroup S/∼o is not cancellative (equivalently, it fails left or right cancellation)?
justification: The draft is aiming not at the original broad Problem 6.16 itself, but at the residual open question that remains after this paper’s contribution. In §1 the paper restates Problem 6.16 for Otto conjugacy; in §6, Example 6.1, it constructs an infinite semigroup with ∼o a congruence and noncancellative quotient; and in §9 it records the unresolved finite analogue as Problem 9.4. The refined question therefore keeps the finite-existence focus and adds only the standard meanings of “congruence” and “cancellative” needed to make the question fully self-contained, without broadening the scope beyond the paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
